title: Red warning issued for strong winds, rough seas - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - The Department of Meteorology has issued a red warning for strong winds and rough seas off the coasts extending from Kankesanthurai to Kalpitiya via Mannar and from Hambantota to Pottuvil.

The Department said the sea areas off the coasts extending from Kankesanthurai to Kalpitiya via Mannar and from Hambantota to Pottuvil will be very rough at times with strong gusty winds up to 60 to 70 kmph.

Naval and fishing communities have been advised not to venture into these sea areas until further notice.

The sea areas off the coasts extending from Trincomalee to Kankesanthurai via Mullaittivu and Kalpitiya to Hambantota via Colombo and Galle will be rough at times with strong gusty winds up to 50 to 60 kmph.

The wave height is expected to increase about 2.0 to 2.5 metres in the sea areas off the coast extending from Mannar to Pottuvil via Colombo, Galle and Hambantota.

title: Glasgow Commonwealth Games Kalinga Kumarage qualifies for 400m  Semi-finals - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Kalinga Kumarage

By Susil Premalal

Sri Lankan sprinter Kalinga Kumarage booked his place in the men’s 400m semi-finals at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games after an impressive performance in the opening round.

The athletics competition is being held from July 27 to August 2, with Sri Lanka represented by 19 athletes.

Competing in Heat 5 of the first round, Kumarage finished second in a time of 46.28 seconds to secure automatic qualification for the semi-finals. Based on the overall first-round results, he ranked 11th among the qualifiers.

The men’s 400m semi-final is scheduled to take place at 5.40 p.m. (Sri Lanka time) today (30).

Sri Lanka’s other entrant in the event, Kalhara Indupa, was unable to compete after sustaining an injury before the team departed for Glasgow.

In the men’s 200m, Aruna Darshana finished fourth in Heat 7 with a time of 20.96 seconds, while Malith Thamel placed second in Heat 10 in 20.99 seconds. However, neither athlete progressed to the semi-finals.

Meanwhile, Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallist and Paris 2024 Paralympic bronze medallist Palitha Bandara is scheduled to compete in the Men’s Discus Throw F42–44/F61–64 final on the morning of July 30.

Bandara enters the event as one of Sri Lanka’s strongest medal hopes. His personal best in the discus throw stands at 44.20 metres.

title: Sri Lanka collects over 43 containers of plastic pellets from MSC Elsa 3 spill - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - The Marine Environment Protection Authority (MEPA) said that more than 43 containers worth of plastic pellets which washed ashore following the sinking of the MSC Elsa 3 vessel off the Kerala coast had been collected so far.

MEPA Chairman Samantha Gunasekara said the plastic pellets continue to wash ashore along the coastline from the Jaffna islands to Galle, with the situation worsening due to the monsoon season.

He said that around 1,800 workers have been deployed for the removal of the plastic pellets, with the costs being covered by the relevant shipping company.

Meanwhile, preparations are underway to estimate the compensation required for the damage caused to Sri Lanka’s marine ecosystem due to the sinking of the vessel. The expert committee appointed for this purpose also held a meeting yesterday, the chairman said.

The Liberian-flagged container ship MSC Elsa 3 sank on May 25, 2025, after developing a water leak in waters located about 38 nautical miles off the coast of Kerala, India. The vessel was carrying 643 containers at the time of the incident.

title: Don’t Put Judges in a Difficult Position: Opposition MP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - While noting that a time will come when judges in Sri Lanka will have to deliver a judgement on themselves, Opposition MP Dayasiri Jayasekera yesterday said they would be called upon to make a determination on a proposal to extend their retirement age by two years, a decision that would benefit them.

"The government should not put the judges into a difficult situation by making them give a determination which will benefit them," the MP told journalists.

He also said the President should hold a referendum to seek the views of the people on the matter.

"A referendum should be called for to seek the view of the people because the retirement age of judges is a constitutional amendment. President Anura Kumara Dissanayake should therefore call a referendum as it was done by late President J. R. Jayewardene," he said.

Asked about the allegation by government members that the opposition is disturbed because legal cases are to be filed against some politicians, including the Rajapaksa's, Jayasekera said the government could file cases against anyone but should not interfere with the judiciary.

title: Wild Elephants push down garden wall to eat jak - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Kanchana Kumara

Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Three wild elephants which had entered Sigiriya town in the early hours of last morning had pushed down a parapet wall of a home garden to eat jak fruit from a tree.

The owner said a herd of three wild elephants had entered the garden at about 3.30am after pushing down the 200ft long garden wall and eaten jak fruits.

They said they informed the wildlife officers on the incident but to no avail. They pointed out that their house is in close proximity to the Wildlife Department office, but they came out with the excused that they were not in a position to visit the scene for want of a vehicle.

Residents of Sigriya area said they have been facing the threat of wild elephants since long and that they are living in constant fear. They pointed out that groups of tourists visiting Sigiriya area and frequenting the roads during day and night are at the mercy of the marauding jumbos.

title: NPP cannot take disciplinary action against me : Lal Wijenayake - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - National Peoples Power (NPP) cannot take disciplinary action against me as I have not gone against any decision made by the party, NPP executive committee member Lal Wijenayake said yesterday.

" NPP had not discussed the proposal to extend the retirement age of Judges in any of its committee's and had not made a decision on it. Therefore the party cannot take any disciplinary action against me" lawyer Wijenayake told journalists.

" This is not a battle against the government but a struggle to safeguard the independence of the Judiciary. No lawyer could practice his or her profession in a situation where there is no independence of Judiciary. A lawyer would not be able to practice if he is aware of the outcome of any case" he added.

Wijenayake earlier said that the NPP leadership had asked him to be silent about the extending the retirement age of judges.

Wijenayake was among the lawyers who were present at yesterday 's special meeting of the Bar Association.

title: Ministry directs CAA to intensify action against overpriced blood tests at private hospitals - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - While expressing concern over reports that some private hospitals are charging patients above the government-approved prices for Full Blood Count (FBC) tests, the Ministry of Health has directed relevant authorities to intensify inspections and raids on private healthcare institutions.

This happens against the backdrop, where the country continues to grapple with a surge in dengue cases.

Sources said the Ministry is concerned that patients suspected of having dengue, who often require repeated FBC tests to monitor their platelet counts and overall condition, could face an unnecessary financial burden if hospitals fail to adhere to the regulated prices.

In response, the Ministry has requested the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) and other relevant authorities to intensify inspections and raids on private healthcare institutions to ensure compliance with the government-controlled pricing, the sources added.

The move follows the recent conviction of a private hospital in Vavuniya for overcharging patients for an FBC test.

According to the CAA, the violation was detected during a raid conducted by its investigation officers, who found that the hospital had charged patients more than the government-approved price for the laboratory test.

Following the investigation, the Authority instituted legal proceedings before the Vavuniya Magistrate’s Court, which subsequently imposed a fine of Rs. 500,000 on the hospital for violating the government-controlled price regulations.

the CAA said that under Order No. 67 issued in terms of Section 20(5) of the Consumer Affairs Authority Act, No. 09 of 2003, the maximum charge for a Full Blood Count (FBC) test, including the report, is Rs. 400, while the maximum charge for a Dengue NS1 Antigen test, including the report, is Rs. 1,200.

title: Late IGP borrowed security officer’s weapon, claiming he wanted to examine it: Court told - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Upali Ananda

Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - The security officer of the late IGP C.D. Wickramaratne, testifying at the magisterial inquiry into the death of the former IGP, told court that the late IGP had borrowed his duty weapon and ammunition, claiming that he wanted to examine it.

Sergeant (697) Susantha testifying before Kaduwela Magistrate Aruna Indrajith Buddhadasa on Tuesday (28) said that it was unusual as Mr. Wickramaratne had never asked for his duty weapon before.

Western Province (South) Investigation Unit led evidence at the inquiry.

‘ I count a service of more than 16 years as the Private Security Officer of the former IGP, but he has never asked me for my duty weapon to be checked. However, on the day of the incident, he wanted my duty weapon and after obtaining my duty weapon he asked for ammunition as well. Whenever he went out for exercises, he would put on shoes but on that fateful day he was not wearing shoes. He never took bottles of water when going out for exercises. After I gave him the pistol and ammunition, he told me to bring him a bottle of water. Just as I stepped out, I heard the report of pistol shots, and I rushed to the scene to find him lying on the floor. I with the help of others in the household rushed him to the Mulleriyawa hospital. Later I learnt that he had died.” Sergeant Susantha further submitted.

Magistrate ordered police to refer the pistol and the spent cartridges to the Government Analyst for report.

The JMO Mulleriyawa Base Hospital had returned an open verdict regarding the death of the former IGP.

title: Fleet of 104 Metro buses arrives - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Another fleet of 104 new buses for Metro Transit, a subsidiary of the Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB), has arrived in the country.

According to officials, the new fleet is expected to enhance the efficiency and quality of public transport services across Sri Lanka.

They had announced earlier that the buses will be equipped with card-based electronic fare payment systems and are expected to be deployed for passenger services by September 20.

title: Govt should be judged by its actions - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Responding to a question on whether the government is determined to proceed with extending the retirement age of superior court judges, Justice Minister Harshana Nanayakkara said that the government should be judged by its actions.

However, he declined to make any further comment on the matter.

“You have to judge us by our actions,” he said, adding that he was acting in accordance with the principle of collective Cabinet responsibility.

Asked to comment on the resolution adopted by the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) opposing the move, the Minister again declined to comment but said he was prepared to convey the organisation’s views to the Cabinet.

“I should not comment on the BASL today. I have not watched their programme and I know very little about it. I am only carrying out collective Cabinet responsibility. Whatever ideas they bring to me, I will take them to the Cabinet,” he said.

The government has already obtained Cabinet approval to amend the Constitution to extend the retirement age of superior court judges.

Article 107(5) of the Constitution states: “The age of retirement of Judges of the Supreme Court shall be sixty-five years and of Judges of the Court of Appeal shall be sixty-three years.”

Following Cabinet approval, steps have been initiated to draft the necessary legislation to increase the retirement age of superior court judges by two years.

The move has already drawn opposition from the BASL, the professional body representing around 26,000 lawyers. The Association convened a special meeting yesterday and adopted a resolution expressing its opposition to the proposed amendment.

The BASL has argued that the proposal could undermine public confidence in the independence, impartiality and integrity of the superior courts.

The Commonwealth Lawyers Association has also cautioned that even the perception of interference with judicial tenure could damage the reputation of Sri Lanka’s judicial system and affect confidence in the independence of the judiciary.

summary: Myanmar courts have sentenced nine activists to up to 37 years in prison for participating in a protest that urged the public to boycott last December’s elections.

title: Palitha Bandara wins Sri Lanka’s first medal at 2026 Commonwealth Games - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 30 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka’s Palitha Bandara secured the country’s first medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games after claiming silver in the men’s discus throw F42-44/F61-64 para athletics final.

The silver medal marks Bandara’s second consecutive Commonwealth Games podium finish in the event, having also claimed silver at the Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games.

title: Kamindu guides Kaps to crucial LPL win - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
July.30 (Mirror Sports) - Colombo Kaps boosted their Lanka Premier League 2026 playoff hopes after holding their nerve to defeat Dambulla Sixers by four wickets in a high-scoring contest at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium on Wednesday

Set a target of 175, the Kaps attacked from the outset through Rubin Hermann, whose aggressive 48 from 26 balls put the chase firmly on track. Captain Kamindu Mendis then produced a calm 39 to steady the innings before Ben McDermott (33) and Sadeera Samarawickrama (26) combined to carry Colombo over the line with six balls remaining.

The Sixers had earlier built a competitive total of 174 for 5 after another classy display from Reeza Hendricks. The South African opener struck 80 from 54 deliveries, registering his third fifty of the tournament, while Gulbadin Naib's unbeaten 33 from just 13 balls gave Dambulla a late surge. Shahnawaz Dahani finished as Colombo's most successful bowler with two wickets.

Dambulla fought back through Dushmantha Chameera and Akila Dananjaya, who claimed two wickets each, but the Kaps held their composure to seal an important victory and keep their momentum alive in the race for the knockout stage.

Brief Scores

Dambulla Sixers – 174/5 (20 overs)

Reeza Hendricks 80 (54), Gulbadin Naib 33* (13), Sikandar Raza 23; Shahnawaz Dahani 2/41.

Colombo Kaps – 177/6 (19 overs)

Rubin Hermann 48 (26), Kamindu Mendis 39, Ben McDermott 33, Sadeera Samarawickrama 26; Dushmantha Chameera 2/32, Akila Dananjaya 2/32.

Result: Colombo Kaps won by four wickets.

title: Palestinian tourist killed in parasailing accident off Bentota - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Bentota, July 29 (Daily Mirror): A 31-year-old Palestinian woman was killed after a parasail reportedly crashed into the sea off the Bentota coast this evening (29), police said.

According to Bentota Police, the accident occurred when a parasail operated by an organisation based along the Bentota coastal road plunged into the sea during a flight.

The Palestinian tourist, who was on board the parasail, died in the incident, while the operator, a Colombian national, survived.

The victim's body has been placed at the Nagoda Hospital mortuary for a post-mortem examination.

Bentota Police have launched an investigation to determine the exact cause of the accident.
